review_notes: I read the whole file and searched the repo for outside uses of its API. Only `LpDual.dual_separable` is used elsewhere (FullDual.lean). So the simp interface is mostly internal. The two `@[simp]` lemmas, `finite_apply` and `finite_single`, are oriented sensibly and don't compete. I found no cycle or unwanted expansion. The one weakness is the unannotated `dualInclude_apply` and `dualHead_apply`, which only matters for future use. I can't run Lean, so this is low-to-moderate confidence.

findings.excerpt:
lemma dualInclude_apply (i : ι) (x : StrongDual ℝ (E i)) (v : lp E p) :
    dualInclude E p i x v=x (v i) := rfl
findings.problem: `finite_apply` and `finite_single` are `@[simp]`, but the simp lemmas for the two definitions built on the same API are not. `dualInclude_apply` is a `rfl` evaluation lemma whose RHS `x (v i)` is strictly simpler than the LHS. `dualHead_apply` is the canonical unfolding of `dualHead` to a finite sum of `x (lp.single p i (v i))`. Neither is tagged. `dualInclude` and `dualHead` are plain `def`s, so `simp` cannot see through them. Every use needs a hand-written `simp only [dualHead, sum_apply, dualInclude_apply, ...]` followed by `rfl`, as in the proof of `dualHead_apply`. Callers such as `dual_approximation` also go through `rw [dualHead_apply]`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `dualInclude_apply` as `@[simp]`. It is non-looping and strictly simplifying. Consider `@[simp]` on `dualHead_apply` too, or keep it as a named lemma and document it as the intended unfolding. Then the body of `dualHead_apply` can rely on `simp` with the other simp lemmas instead of the `simp only [...]; rfl` pair.
findings.benefit: Evaluations of `dualHead E p C x v` and `dualInclude E p i x v` normalize to the sum of `x (lp.single p i (v i))` terms or to `x (v i)`. This is the same normal form that `finite_single` and `finite_apply` already target. Future users get this from plain `simp` and no longer need an explicit lemma list.
